notes:
This map models employed residents and workplace demand, rather than total population. Workplace totals come from SGIS 100 m employee grids, based on the National Business Survey/Economic Census. Employed-resident demand is constrained by the origin totals in the observed representative-weekday Seoul Capital Area commuting O/D data; SGIS 100 m population grids are used to distribute those employed-resident totals spatially.

For each 100 m grid cell, resident and workplace totals are allocated to OpenStreetMap building footprints. Allocation uses footprint area, building-use suitability, and local activity mix; a nearest-building fallback is used where no suitable building is available. The resulting building demand is aggregated into representative 200 m demand nodes.

Commute flows use the observed administrative origin–destination matrix for ten representative weekdays in the Seoul Capital Area. The matrix is reconciled with IPF/RAS so origin totals, destination totals, and administrative-zone flows remain consistent, then disaggregated to the demand nodes. O/D zones are primarily dong-level within Seoul; some outer-capital-area zones are necessarily coarser (si/gun/gu or provincial level).

Airport, university, and hospital demand are added separately as special trip generators. They do not replace or alter the census-based workplace, employed-resident, or administrative commuting inputs. Route geometries are calculated with OSRM.
